reference: OpenSSH sftp supplies independent unsupported-option rejection statuses only. The documented command-stream transport, implementation description, and custom help are project contracts, not OpenSSH help or protocol byte parity. All transport and session operations remain deferred.
coverage: Independent unsupported-option failure statuses for -V, -Z, and an unsupported long option; all reject before any endpoint or session exists.
Custom -h/--help and Bash registration/transport-description metadata; these do not count as operation coverage.
exclusions: No connection, authentication, endpoint, key, listener, remote subprocess, DNS, or network operation is executed.
Even local session verbs require an initial remote pwd and remain deferred because of this transport dependency, not because ordinary private file writes are unsafe.
No OpenSSH help/version banner equality or SFTP protocol compatibility is claimed.

cases.purpose: Compare rejection of the unsupported -V option with OpenSSH sftp(1); both clients stop during option parsing before connection setup.
Unsupported -Z is rejected without a host or option operand; no transport path is reachable.
Unsupported long option is rejected before any transport or endpoint handling.
Verify that this command is registered as a Bash builtin, using Bash's documented type -t contract.
Check that Bash help publishes the documented transport description, prompt heading, and final supported verbs from sftp_doc.
cases.script:
help_text=$(help sftp)
[[ $help_text == *"Interactive sftp(1) client over the sshd command-stream transport."* ]]
[[ $help_text == *"Supported verbs in the interactive prompt:"* ]]
[[ $help_text == *"rename, chmod, help, ?, bye, quit, exit."* ]]
printf 'documented sftp help available\n'

cases.purpose: Exercise initial pwd, relative and quoted cd, subsequent remote ls, and batch termination against a controlled remote tree.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable SSH peer that accepts only the candidate's BASHSSH1 command framing and an independent OpenSSH SFTP server mock backed by a small relative fixture tree. Session startup calls remote pwd before reading verbs. The user forbids network activity here, so this operation comparison is deferred.

cases.purpose: Exercise lpwd, lcd, and lls against private relative fixture directories after establishing a session.
cases.reason: Although these verbs act locally, sftp first requires a successful remote pwd, so they cannot be reached safely without a peer. A future disposable mock must provide deterministic pwd and keep lls/lcd paths inside the fixture tree, with OpenSSH batch-mode output as the independent reference.

cases.purpose: Compare get and put for a small binary payload, explicit local/remote names with spaces, and resulting file bytes on both sides.
cases.reason: Requires an isolated peer plus an independent SFTP server mock that supports file open/read/write/close and confines paths to a disposable fixture tree. No network peer is run in this suite; payload and tree parity remain unverified.

cases.purpose: Compare mkdir/rmdir, rename, chmod, and rm effects and representative missing-path failures using only private relative names.
cases.reason: These sftp verbs mutate the remote filesystem and also require the initial remote pwd. A future disposable SSH/SFTP mock must implement the same operations for the candidate and OpenSSH reference, expose final mode/content/tree snapshots, and contain all mutations to a temporary fixture tree. No remote mutation is attempted here.

cases.purpose: Compare -h output/status channels with OpenSSH; the custom documented help remains a separate contract and this deliberate CLI difference stays visible.
